subject.title: AI safety taxonomy: plugin-emitted detectors and evals

question: Should OpenClaw standardize a purpose-built AI-safety event facade and manifest permission contract on top of the generic diagnostics dispatcher after the core schema is approved?
rationale: This creates a durable third-party Plugin SDK and manifest contract, and the appropriate specialization, trust policy, and privacy boundary cannot be inferred mechanically from the generic emitter.

options.title: Approve sequenced facade
options.body: Approve the specialized facade in principle, require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107158 to settle the schema first, and then review the linked PR against the canonical diagnostics boundary.

options.title: Use generic diagnostics only
options.body: Decline a safety-specific SDK surface and instead document approved `DiagnosticEventInput` variants and generic plugin emission.

options.title: Keep taxonomy external
options.body: Leave detector and evaluation event conventions entirely to plugins or external observability systems without a new core contract.

recommendation.title: Approve sequenced facade
recommendation.body: Approve the specialized facade in principle, require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107158 to settle the schema first, and then review the linked PR against the canonical diagnostics boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history places central plugin registry, metadata, and SDK-boundary decisions in this contributor's area.
